scope: PR #1 on akashbhardwaj01nagarro/ai-sdlc-demo-app (001-approval-limits at ca0ab9b into main), 167 files: feature code (backend/src), tests (backend/tests, e2e), agent tooling (.claude hooks, settings, agents and non-speckit skills, .githooks, scripts), and a secrets and personal-data scan of all 17,003 added lines including .specify/, speckit skills, docs/mutation/, docs/evidence/ and lock files. Merged from review-rules, review-tests and review-security; review prompt from the pr-review skill, standing in for the workshop's prompt, which was not available.

findings.title: Rounding the amount to cents inside ApprovalService passes every test (FR-001, FR-003)
findings.evidence: From review-tests T-02, confirmed. Every amount in ApprovalServiceTests has at most two decimals (100m, 100.00m, 50000.00m, 50000.01m, 60000.00m, 500000.00m, 500000.01m, 600000.00m), and so do both Playwright tests (60000, 640000). The sub-cent cases 50000.001m and 500000.001m exist only in ApprovalPolicyTests (lines 72, 84, 169), which call ApprovalPolicy.Decide directly. So passing decimal.Round(invoice.Amount, 2) to Decide at ApprovalService.cs:59 passes the whole suite, yet lets a Manager approve 50,000.004 (FR-001) and one Director approve 500,000.004 alone (FR-003). The API accepts any positive decimal (InvoicesController.cs:55), and AGENTS.md says never to round before comparing. The US1 review accepted the same mutant one layer down (docs/evidence/test-review/us1.md:28).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a RefusedAttempts row for demo.manager at 50000.001m expecting AmountAboveRoleLimit and the exact message with '50,000.001', and also run the service test for a first approval above 500,000.00 at 500000.001m, asserting that a Director's approval only records FirstApprovedBy and the invoice stays pending.
findings.proposed_reason: Two data rows close a gap in the dual-control rule. The exposure is limited to amounts with more than two decimals, so a human may lower the severity, but only a test closes the gap.

findings.title: No test covers Admin passing the approvals role gate (Admin approval refused by the Domain, Admin rejection allowed)
findings.evidence: From review-tests T-01, plus the test clause of review-security S-07, confirmed. This PR changed the gate from [RequireRole('Approver', 'Admin')] to Manager, Director, Admin. The unit tests reference only the Domain project (InvoiceApp.Tests.csproj:15), and neither Playwright test signs in as demo.admin or rejects an invoice (e2e/pages/ApprovalsPage.ts has no reject method). Dropping Admin from the gate at line 10 therefore passes every test, yet Admin could no longer reject (FR-007; the spec assumption that Admin keeps rejecting and deleting), and an Admin approval would get the gate's 403 without code or invoice instead of the Domain's RoleCannotApprove reason (FR-005, FR-006, US1 acceptance scenario 5). The US1 review deferred this API-level check on a manual smoke test (docs/evidence/test-review/us1.md:31) with no follow-up issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Playwright test on the existing page objects: demo.admin approves a fresh pending invoice and gets 403 with exactly { error: 'Approval refused: invoice <id> cannot be approved by the Admin role. Only Managers and Directors can approve invoices.', code: 'RoleCannotApprove' } and the invoice unchanged after a reload; then rejects it with a reason and gets 200, status Rejected, decidedBy demo.admin. Add a reject method to ApprovalsPage with role and label locators.
findings.proposed_reason: One end-to-end test on existing page objects protects an acceptance scenario and FR-007. The earlier deferral rests on a manual check nobody can repeat, and a deferral needs a follow-up issue, which the fork cannot hold while issues are disabled.

findings.title: guard-git lets common command forms reach the upstream workshop repository
findings.evidence: From review-security S-01, confirmed by calling the exported evaluate() on each string (none was executed). It denies 'git push upstream main' and 'gh pr create --repo NITIN1670/ai-sdlc-demo-app', but allows: '& gh pr create --repo <upstream>' (PowerShell call operator), 'env gh issue create --repo <upstream>', a push inside 'bash -c', '(git push upstream main)', 'echo x & git push upstream main', 'gh pr create --repo <fork> --repo <upstream>' (gh takes the last value, optionValue at lines 65-73 the first), 'GH_REPO=<upstream> gh api -X POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues -f title=x', 'gh api -XPOST repos/<upstream>/issues -ftitle=x', 'gh api repos/<upstream>/issues --raw-field=title=x', 'gh release create v1 --repo <upstream>', 'gh pr update-branch 1 --repo <upstream>', 'git -c remote.origin.pushurl=<upstream URL> push origin' and 'git remote set-url origin <upstream URL>'. Causes: only the first token of a segment counts (lines 146-151), a single '&' does not split segments (line 21), leading VAR= assignments are skipped unread (line 146), gh api writes are recognised only by an exact '-X'/'--method' or an exact field flag (lines 112-113), and only the pr and issue actions in GH_WRITE_ACTIONS are checked (lines 12-15, 118). The upstream repository is public with issues enabled, so these gh writes need no write access. AGENTS.md says a hook blocks anything aimed at the upstream repository. Mitigations outside the PR: this clone's upstream push URL is DISABLED, and the project defines no permission allow rules (no permissions block in .claude/settings.json, no .claude/settings.local.json), so in the default mode a human still approves each command.
findings.suggested_fix: Look for git and gh anywhere in a segment (after '&', call operators, env/command wrappers, 'bash -c' strings, subshell parentheses) and also split on a single '&'; require every --repo/-R value, including '=' forms, to be the fork; treat gh api as a write for any -X/--method spelling other than GET and any -f/-F/--field/--raw-field/--input form; deny GH_REPO, GIT_CONFIG_*, '-c remote.*' and 'git remote set-url/add' that point at the upstream; deny gh release, label and repo writes against it. Add each form above to guard-git.test.mjs.
findings.proposed_reason: The hook is the documented control behind the fork-only rule, and several bypasses (PowerShell '&', a repeated --repo, gh api shorthands) need no intent to evade. Given the permission prompt and the disabled push URL, a human may lower it to minor.

findings.title: Roles other than Manager, Director and Admin are refused by the API role gate, not the Domain: no code, no invoice, and Admin listed as allowed
findings.evidence: From review-rules R-01 and review-security S-07 (merged), confirmed. The class-level [RequireRole(Manager, Director, Admin)] answers every other role (the legacy Approver, 'manager', an empty or unknown role) before ApprovalPolicy runs. RequireRoleAttribute.cs:27 returns 403 { error: 'Your role (X) cannot do this. Allowed roles: Manager, Director, Admin.' }: no code, no invoice, and Admin listed as allowed, although ApprovalPolicy refuses Admin. FR-006 says every other role, including unknown roles, MUST be refused under FR-005, whose reason names the invoice and the rule with its facts; AGENTS.md asks for 403 { error, code } on a refused approval and says approval authority is decided in Domain, not by the role gate. ApprovalPolicy.LimitFor (ApprovalPolicy.cs:71-76) already refuses these roles with RoleCannotApprove, but only Admin reaches it. Both paths fail closed and change nothing, and no shipped account has another role (appsettings.json), so reaching it takes a configuration change. contracts/approvals-api.md:17 documents the gate reply, which conflicts with FR-006.
findings.suggested_fix: Move [RequireRole(ApprovalRoles.Manager, ApprovalRoles.Director, ApprovalRoles.Admin)] from the class to the Reject action, so every signed-in approval attempt reaches ApprovalPolicy and gets 403 { error, code: 'RoleCannotApprove' } naming the invoice; narrow contracts/approvals-api.md:17 to reject.
findings.proposed_reason: One attribute and one contract line put approval authority in Domain as AGENTS.md requires. As an FR-005 finding it can only be dismissed with a test that proves it wrong.

findings.title: FR-004 under simultaneous requests depends on the repository being a DI singleton
findings.evidence: From review-rules R-03, confirmed. _decisionGate = DecisionGates.GetOrCreateValue(repository) gives one lock per repository instance (lines 15 and 30). It serialises every decision at HEAD only because Program.cs:14 registers IInvoiceRepository as a singleton (ApprovalService is scoped, Program.cs:16), as the comment at lines 12-14 says. A scoped or transient repository, the usual lifetime of a database-backed one, gives each request its own lock and silently drops the FR-004 guarantee for simultaneous requests; no test would fail, because the concurrency tests share one FakeInvoiceRepository and there is no API-level test. An in-process lock also cannot cover two app instances. review-rules showed it holds at HEAD over HTTP: 20 parallel approvals by one Director gave one 200 and 19 SameApproverTwice refusals. research.md R6 (lines 61-62) notes optimistic concurrency with a version field as the alternative for a real database.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the lock for the in-memory demo and say next to the singleton registration in Program.cs that FR-004 depends on it; with the first persistent repository, move the read-decide-write guard into the store (a conditional update on Status and FirstApprovedBy, or a version column).
findings.proposed_reason: Correct at HEAD, and the guard must be redesigned with persistence anyway (research.md R6). As an FR-004 finding it cannot be dismissed without a test, and a deferral needs a follow-up issue, so issues must first be enabled on the fork.

findings.title: Delete bypasses the decision gate, so an approval racing a delete answers 200 Approved for an invoice that is not stored
findings.evidence: From review-rules R-02, confirmed in the code. Submit, Approve and Reject run inside the decision gate (ApprovalService.cs:35, 53, 88), but Delete calls _repository.Remove(id) directly (InvoicesController.cs:74-75). Approve keeps the live object from Find (ApprovalService.cs:55); if Remove lands before Update, the service writes Approved to an orphaned object, InMemoryInvoiceRepository.Update skips the missing id silently (InMemoryInvoiceRepository.cs:56-57), and the controller answers 200 with an Approved invoice that no longer exists. Reject and Submit behave the same way. No FR-001 to FR-005 rule breaks (the invoice ends deleted, not wrongly approved). InvoicesController.cs is unchanged by this PR, and main had the same race without any gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete through the gate (an ApprovalService.Delete that locks the decision gate, called from InvoicesController.Delete), or have Update report a missing invoice so the decision ends in 404.
findings.proposed_reason: Pre-existing, outside spec 001, with a narrow window; track it in a follow-up issue once issues are enabled on the fork.

findings.title: No test asserts the 404 and 409 answers, and the new 403 mapping is tested only by Playwright
findings.evidence: From review-tests T-03, confirmed. The test project references only Domain (InvoiceApp.Tests.csproj:15), so dotnet test never runs Handle or the role gate. The 403 { error, code } mapping this PR adds (lines 15-19) is asserted only by Playwright (approval-limits.spec.ts:32-33, two-approvers.spec.ts:66-67), which the per-commit dotnet test run does not include. No test at any level asserts 404 for an unknown invoice or 409 for a non-pending one (contracts/approvals-api.md:14-15); the unit tests stop at the Domain exceptions (ApprovalServiceTests.cs:450, 476). The 404 and 409 catches (lines 20-27) are unchanged from main.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an API test project (WebApplicationFactory<Program>, one test class per controller) covering each row of contracts/approvals-api.md: 200 final and first approval, 404, 409, 403 with each ApprovalRefusal code, the gate's 403, and 401.
findings.proposed_reason: The 404/409 mapping predates this PR and a new test project is separate work; the new 403 mapping is covered end to end. A deferral needs issues enabled on the fork.

findings.title: guard-git allows the command when it cannot read the hook input
findings.evidence: From review-security S-02, confirmed. Unparseable stdin throws at line 164 and the catch (lines 183-189) only writes to stderr; a missing or non-string tool_input.command returns at line 166. Either way no deny is printed and the command runs, and guard-git.test.mjs:73-75 pins garbage input as allowed. Reach is limited: Claude Code sends JSON with tool_input.command for both Bash and PowerShell (the logged PowerShell calls carry command), so this matters only if that input format changes.
findings.suggested_fix: When the input cannot be parsed or has no string command, print a deny decision ('guard-git could not read the command') and change guard-git.test.mjs:73-75 to expect it.
findings.proposed_reason: A guard should fail closed; it is a few lines in the file that R-03 and R-09 already change.

findings.title: Force-push and hook-skipping checks miss a '+' refspec, a combined '-n' and '-c core.hooksPath'
findings.evidence: From review-security S-03, confirmed with evaluate(): 'git push origin +main' (a force push through the refspec; isForce at line 81 looks only at flags), 'git commit -anm x' (-n among combined short flags; line 103 matches only an exact '-n') and 'git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -m x' (the -c value is skipped unread at lines 129-131, which switches off .githooks/commit-msg) are all allowed. The hook header (lines 2-5) says force pushes and --no-verify are denied, and commit-conventions/SKILL.md:23 forbids both.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a push refspec starting with '+' as a force push, detect 'n' among the combined short flags of git commit, deny core.hooksPath set through -c or GIT_CONFIG_*, and add the cases to guard-git.test.mjs.
findings.proposed_reason: Each is a one-line check in the same file and test file as R-03.

findings.title: Redaction misses non-Windows home paths and several credential formats
findings.evidence: From review-security S-05, confirmed by running redactText on fake samples. Windows and Git Bash home paths become '~', and 'password="[REDACTED]" and email addresses are redacted, but these pass unchanged: '/Users/<name>' (macOS), '/home/<name>' (Linux), '/mnt/c/Users/<name>' (WSL; the lookbehind at line 37 rejects it), a PEM private-key header, a JWT, 'Authorization: Basic ...', a JSON token field inside tool-output text (SECRET_KEY at line 18 applies only to parsed object keys, and the text rule at line 27 has no token or secret), and '--password <value>'. A malformed redact.local.json is ignored silently (lines 56-58). The header (lines 1-3) promises that secrets and personal data are replaced and home directories become '~', and ai-logs/ is due to be committed (tasks.md T038).
findings.suggested_fix: Add rules for /Users/<name>, /home/<name>, /mnt/<drive>/Users/<name>, PEM private-key blocks, JWTs, Basic auth, token/secret/access_token/refresh_token in key=value and JSON text, and --password <value>; warn on stderr when redact.local.json does not parse; extend redact.test.mjs and the log-auditor checklist to match.
findings.proposed_reason: The log is meant to be published, so the credential rules should be in place before ai-logs/ is committed. The non-Windows path rules could be deferred, because this log was produced on Windows.

findings.title: Read-only agents can still write through Bash, and pr-reviewer can start writer subagents
findings.evidence: From review-security S-06, confirmed. pr-reviewer, review-rules, review-tests, review-security, test-critic and log-auditor are described as read-only and disallow Write and Edit, but each has Bash (pr-reviewer.md:4), which can edit files, commit, or post 'gh pr comment --repo <fork>' (guard-git allows writes to the fork). pr-reviewer's Agent tool is not restricted, so it can start domain-implementer, test-author or e2e-author, which have Write and Edit. .claude/settings.json has no permissions block and no hook restricts tools by agent_type, so read-only rests on the prompts and the permission prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a PreToolUse hook keyed on agent_type (as check-report already does) that denies state-changing Bash and PowerShell commands for the read-only agents, and let pr-reviewer start only the three reviewers.
findings.proposed_reason: Needs a decision on which commands the reviewers legitimately need (gh pr diff, git diff, dotnet test, Stryker); it hardens the tooling rather than the feature, and the permission prompt still applies in the default mode. A deferral needs issues enabled on the fork.

findings.title: A refusal step checks only the exception type
findings.evidence: From review-tests T-04, confirmed. In Approve_RefusedAttemptLeavesTheInvoiceApprovableByAnAllowedApprover the Manager's refused attempt is a bare Assert.Throws<ApprovalRefusedException> (lines 432-433): no reason code, no snapshot taken before it, and no UpdateCount == 0 after it, which AGENTS.md (Tests) asks of a refusal. No wrong implementation escapes, because the RefusedAttempts row at line 354 checks the same input (Manager, 50,000.01, no first approval) in full.
findings.suggested_fix: Take InvoiceSnapshot.Of before the refused attempt and assert Reason == AmountAboveRoleLimit, an equal snapshot and UpdateCount == 0 before the Director approves.
findings.proposed_reason: Four lines bring the test in line with the AGENTS.md refusal convention. Dismissing it with the row at line 354 as evidence is also defensible.

findings.title: check-report neither validates nor records a SubagentStop retry, and lets unreadable input through
findings.evidence: From review-security S-04, confirmed. planCheck returns null when stop_hook_active is set (line 184), so a retried final message is neither validated nor logged as a ReportCheck event, and a parse error ends in the catch at lines 221-231 with exit 0. This is deliberate: the header (lines 7-9) blocks once so a subagent cannot loop on the stop hook. Hand-backs, the way subagents return reports in this harness, are validated at PreToolUse and denied when malformed (lines 177-182).
findings.suggested_fix: On a retry, validate and append a ReportCheck event (for example result 'rejected-unblocked') without blocking, and record a ReportCheck error when the input cannot be parsed.
findings.proposed_reason: Deliberate loop protection documented at check-report.mjs:7-9, and the PreToolUse check denies every malformed hand-back; what remains is a logging gap. A human may prefer defer if the audit trail must show every unvalidated report.

findings.title: A redaction comment contains the local Windows short account name
findings.evidence: From review-security S-08, confirmed. The comment at line 35 uses '<8.3 short name>', the 8.3 short form of this machine's Windows account, as its example. It is the only local account detail that review-security's scan and mine found in the 17,003 added lines: email addresses are noreply or example.com placeholders, token-like strings are test fixtures, and ChangeMe123! appears only for the documented demo accounts. It reveals little beyond the public GitHub login, and redact.test.mjs:35 already uses the neutral SOMEON~1.
findings.proposed_reason: A one-word change that keeps local account names out of committed files.
